  "text": "In the spring, the harbour office ordered new tide tables. Maren checked them against her own and found a difference of four minutes. She corrected the printed sheets in pencil. Nobody asked her why.

There were other things to do. The lighthouse door needed planing. A gutter had come loose above her kitchen. She bought a bag of early potatoes and left them on the windowsill until their pale shoots turned green.

One afternoon Erris came with a school exercise book.

They had been told to ask someone about their work.

Maren put the kettle on.

The girl wanted to know how long she had done it, whether she liked it, and what happened when she went away.

"I haven't been away," Maren said.

Erris wrote this down. Then she rubbed it out so hard the table shook.

"You could," she said.

Maren took two cups from the cupboard. One had belonged to Agnes. She put that one back and chose another.

"Ask me about the boats."

So they talked about draught and depth, about the bar beyond the harbour mouth, about the marks on the wall that let a person measure what was rising.

After the girl left, Maren planted the potatoes. The soil was cold below the surface. She worked until the light went, then stood with her hands loose at her sides.

From the garden she could see the lighthouse window.

She went inside and washed her hands. There was earth beneath her nails, and she took some care over getting it out.

There was time to make supper."
